raw_results.question: Find the top 5 articles with the highest in-degree / out-degree ratio based on CITED relationships, excluding any article with out-degree 0. Report only the titles as a list of strings and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Article)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:CITED]->(:Article)
WITH a, count(r) AS outDeg
WHERE outDeg > 0
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Article)-[r2:CITED]->(a)
WITH a, outDeg, count(r2) AS inDeg
RETURN a.title AS title
ORDER BY toFloat(inDeg) / outDeg DESC, inDeg DESC, outDeg ASC, title ASC
LIMIT 5

raw_results.question: Find the longest citation chain (path) between any two articles following outgoing CITED edges. Report only the length as a number and nothing else.

Build the co-authorship graph where two authors are connected (undirected, unweighted) if they co-authored at least one article. Using the Adamic Adar measure, score the likelihood of future collaboration between Chao Zhang and each of their 2nd-degree co-authors — people who share a 1st-degree co-author with Chao Zhang but have never directly co-authored with them. Report only the top 3 names as a list of strings, breaking ties by name ascending and nothing else.

parameters.query: MATCH (a:Author {name:$name}) RETURN count(a) AS count

// Adamic-Adar scoring for 2nd-degree co-authors of a given author
MATCH (chao:Author {name:$name})
// first-degree co-authors of Chao
MATCH (chao)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(co1:Author)
WITH chao, collect(DISTINCT co1) AS co1s
// compute co-author degree for each co1 in the co-authorship graph
UNWIND co1s AS w
MATCH (w)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(nbr:Author)
WHERE nbr <> w
WITH chao, co1s, w, count(DISTINCT nbr) AS deg
WITH chao, collect({w: w, deg: deg}) AS wdegs, co1s
// candidates: authors who coauthored with a co1 but not with Chao, and are not already direct coauthors
UNWIND co1s AS c1
MATCH (c1)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(cand:Author)
WHERE cand <> chao
  AND NOT cand IN co1s
  AND NOT (chao)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(cand)
WITH chao, wdegs, collect(DISTINCT cand) AS cands
UNWIND cands AS cand
// common neighbors between Chao and candidate in the co-auth graph
MATCH (cand)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(w:Author)
MATCH (chao)<-[:AUTHOR]-(:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(w)
WITH cand, w, wdegs
WITH cand, head([d IN wdegs WHERE d.w = w | d.deg]) AS deg
WITH cand, sum(1.0 / log(toFloat(deg))) AS score
RETURN cand.name AS name, score
ORDER BY score DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 3

raw_results.question: Chao Zhang has never co-authored with certain researchers who nonetheless share a co-author with them. Among these indirect connections, find the 3 most likely future collaborators, where a shared co-author counts more if that co-author has fewer total collaborators overall. Report only the top 3 names as a list of strings, breaking ties by name ascending and nothing else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (a:Author {name: $name})
WITH a
// Collect Chao Zhang's direct co-authors
MATCH (a)<-[:AUTHOR]-(p:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(co:Author)
WITH a, collect(DISTINCT co) AS coauthors
UNWIND coauthors AS x
// Candidates are authors who share a co-author x with a, but are not directly connected to a
MATCH (x)<-[:AUTHOR]-(q:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(b:Author)
WHERE b <> a AND NOT b IN coauthors
WITH DISTINCT a, x, b
// Compute x's total number of unique collaborators (degree in the co-author graph)
MATCH (x)<-[:AUTHOR]-(r:Article)-[:AUTHOR]->(other:Author)
WHERE other <> x
WITH b, x, count(DISTINCT other) AS degX
WITH b, sum(1.0 / toFloat(degX)) AS score
RETURN b.name AS name, score
ORDER BY score DESC, name ASC
LIMIT 3
